title: Quickfire evals 1:1 prep - Wed dry run
content:
Meeting purpose:
- Quick sync with Ethan to triage yesterday's A/B run and pick 2 small experiments to push this sprint. Focus: fix top regressions, validate prompt variants, and decide whether to flip model routing for low-cost tier.

Agenda (15-20m):
1) Quick numbers (2m)
   - A: baseline (gptx-lite-1q8) avg latency 140ms, cost proxy 0.62 units/token
   - B: opt-batched (quantized + batching) avg latency 170ms, cost 0.42 units/token
   - Rerank pass rate: A 7.6% bad outputs, B 11.9% bad outputs (increase mostly in long-instruction cases)

2) Top regressions (5m)
   - Case cluster #1: long multi-step instructions (>400 tokens) -> hallucination on steps 3-5. Examples: denied-step, invented-api-param.
   - Case cluster #2: finance domain numerical formatting -> decimal truncation in B (2 significant digits lost)
   - Root hypothesis: KV-cache evictions + FP8 quantization interplay on longer context. Also look at prompt-tokenization differences (trailing whitespace)

3) Prompt set & ABR (5m)
   - Current prompt set v2026-03-09 has 220 prompts; subset failing = 28. Many are multi-turn.
   - Quick idea: explicit step markers (Step 1:, Step 2:) reduced hallucination in local toy run. Add 4 templated prompts for next run.

4) Decisions & next steps (3-5m)
   - Short experiment A: try model B with forced-step-markers on subset (N=100) -> owner: Samira, run by Friday 3/13. Track hallucination rate + latency delta.
   - Short experiment B: lower KV-cache eviction threshold (increase cache retention window for same-session requests) on opt-batched infra for N=200 long-context prompts -> owner: Ethan, schedule for Thursday 3/13.
   - If either reduces bad outputs by >=40% relative to B baseline, consider enabling B for low-cost tier in canary (10% traffic) next week.

Notes-to-self / quick observations:
- Weird tokenization: some finance prompts have non-breaking space (U+00A0) inserted by copy-paste from spreadsheets; leads to different token counts. Add a pre-cleaning step to prompt pipeline.
- Reranker currently uses cosine similarity threshold 0.62; raising to 0.66 helped one failing case but increased latency. To test: add adaptive thresholding for long prompts only.
- Remember to add examples to the eval dashboard for each regression cluster with before/after diffs and a clear label (hallucination, formatting, omission).

Follow-ups (explicit):
- Samira: create short prompt templates (+4) and push to experiment corpus; write run spec with pass/fail criteria and log IDs. Due: 2026-03-13.
- Ethan: schedule cache retention tweak on opt-batched infra and instrument KV hit/miss metrics. Add rollout guard in infra. Due: 2026-03-14.
- Maya: add failing examples to the eval dashboard and tag with "regression-long-context". Also snapshot tokenization edges. Due: 2026-03-13.
- Ops (cc @infra-oncall): ensure blue/green rollback available for canary if we flip routing. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/310

Open questions (to raise in 1:1 if time):
- Is there a cheap way to detect content that is sensitive to quantization (e.g., precise numeric tables) and force use of baseline model? Policy trigger ideas: long numeric sequences or percent signs?
- How confident are we in the cost proxy units? Need to reconcile with billing delta from yesterday's run. Who can pull token-level billing? (ask finance or billing-api).
- If we enable adaptive rerank threshold, what's the monitoring alert we should set to detect false negatives? Suggest: >=3x increase in user-reported hallucinations or 2% increase in error-rate metric within 1 hour.

Quick checklist for the call:
- [ ] Share A/B top-line numbers (I will paste in chat)
- [ ] Confirm owners & due dates (write as tasks in Linear)
- [ ] Agree on one mitigation to try first (my vote: prompt templates + pre-cleaning)
- [ ] If green, schedule canary playbook draft (ops + SRE)

Lingering thought (brain dump):
- Could we at routing time pick variant based on a cheap heuristic classifier that predicts "quantization-sensitive"? Train a small model on current failure clusters (features: prompt length, numeric token ratio, presence of code blocks, special characters). If high probability -> route to baseline. Low friction, could cut rollback blast radius. Add to backlog if experiments show consistent signal.

Random TODOs (personal):
- Update README for eval-run naming convention (we keep mixing yyyy-mm-dd and dd-mm formats)
- Add short note about non-breaking space sanitizer in prompt docs
- Ping finance for cost-reconciliation job

End of scratchpad.
